title: How to find your first 1,000 users: the seven early-growth strategies from 100+ consumer startups
summary: Lenny reviewed the early growth of 100+ consumer companies and found only seven reliable ways to get the first 1,000 users: friends, targeted strangers, where your audience hangs out, influencers, press, viral content, and physical placement. Pick two or three, focus, and start with the easy inner circle before moving outward.

principles.text: Only seven channels reliably get your first 1,000 users; pick two or three, try them, and focus rather than doing everything.
principles.quote: Like with a menu, your job is to peruse this list, pick two or three items that seem appetizing, and try them. If something works, chow down. If not, try something else.

principles.text: Most startups get nearly all early growth from one or two channels, so focus instead of ordering everything on the menu.
principles.quote: almost every startup finds the vast majority of their early growth from just one or two channels.

principles.text: Start with the easy stuff near the founder (friends, colleagues) and migrate outward only if it isn't working.
principles.quote: So in your decision of where to start, start with the easy stuff and migrate outward if nothing is working.

principles.text: The highest-ROI early channel is going where your super-specific audience already gathers and giving real value, not spam.
principles.quote: The single most popular (over 50%!), effective, and highest-ROI strategy for finding your first 1,000 users is to find an existing gathering spot for your super-specific who

principles.text: Marketplaces should manually recruit targeted strangers on the supply side, because each supplier is valuable enough to justify heavy cold outreach.
principles.quote: this tactic was almost exclusively used by marketplace startups to bootstrap the supply side and rarely used by non-marketplaces. I imagine this is because one unit of supply is worth a lot to a new marketplace

principles.text: Friends are the fastest early source, but only useful if they resemble your super-specific who; don't get discouraged if they aren't.
principles.quote: just don't get discouraged if it doesn't bear fruit, as your friends may not be anything like your super-specific who.
